name: Lauren Brunson
statement:
I see my pieces as expressions of free will, the gift given to humanity by fate. I try to focus on responding to the thoughts and feelings I experience while working on any given piece. I also try to trust hunches or gut-feelings I have about my work any time during the process.
I have found myself to be somewhat experimental in my artistic methods. I seem to be somewhat eager to try new papers, media, and even artistic styles themselves. I try to learn about my abilities and interests as an artist with each new method I employ. I try to express a piece’s mood or message by using different techniques for shading and creating value in attempts to keep things relatively figurative. I keep each medium’s attributes in mind when I decide what to use and how to apply it. I respond to intuitive feelings I have regarding use of color, as well as a sense of balance. This may change based on the message I want to convey or atmosphere I’m trying to create. If a mistake happens during a process, I usually just ‘go with it’; I  try to reflect both an unsettling dose of reality as well as a far-off surrealism in my work-- I suppose it’s a desire to represent the ever-present duality of mankind.
Most recently, I have been exploring themes related to thoughts and feelings I’ve been coping with. I’ve been drawing things I like, such as musicians in varying line and 2-D styles and representations of lyrics I enjoy, even if only recorded as sketches in my sketchbook. I have also been exploring tender subject matter. I’ve personally noticed more psychological subtones in my work, and even blunt representations of my reactions and negative emotions.
In the future, I hope to continue to develop my own personal style and artistic direction, as well as keep learning more about the art of unfamiliar cultures, styles, time periods, and methods.
